executiveSummary: Iran-affiliated actors are actively manipulating PLC logic and HMI/SCADA data across US critical infrastructure, with impacts to Water/Wastewater, Energy, and Government Facilities; immediate OT hardening and removal of internet exposure are required. Security Advisory View Article Russian state-supported LAUNDRY BEAR is exploiting a Zimbra zero-day to exfiltrate mail, credentials, and 2FA codes from defense and government entities, enabling persistence and lateral movement toward OT-adjacent systems. Security Advisory View Article Perimeter VPN/auth weaknesses are under active exploitation: Check Point Remote Access IKEv1 auth bypass and widespread FortiGate credential leakage enable rapid IT-to-OT pivots; disable legacy protocols, rotate credentials, and patch immediately. Alert Alert Edge router exploitation by Russian FSB Center 16 targets SNMP defaults, Cisco Smart Install, and known Cisco CVEs to access critical infrastructure networks; enforce SNMPv3 authPriv, disable SMI, and block management protocols at perimeters. Security Advisory Multiple high-severity OT library/product issues demand urgent patching and segmentation: libIEC61850 RCE/DoS, lib60870 DoS, Weintek HMI credential/permission weaknesses, and Rockwell ThinManager path traversal. ICS Advisory ICS Advisory Active exploitation of GeoServer RCE (CVE-2024-36401) is observed in the wild; GIS servers often underpin municipal/utilities functions—patch and restrict WFS immediately. Supporting Report View Article Chinese-nexus operations leverage covert SOHO/IoT botnets for pre-positioning in critical infrastructure; harden edge devices and hunt for activity from residential IP space. Security Advisory Pro-Russia hacktivists opportunistically abuse exposed VNC on HMIs, causing loss of view and setpoint changes; immediately remove public VNC and enforce MFA via secured jump hosts. Security Advisory Actively exploited Microsoft SharePoint/ADFS flaws threaten enterprise identity and can enable OT pivots; prioritize July KEV-listed fixes and instrumentation for webshells and AMSI detections. Security Advisory KEV Update

descriptions: Initial Access: Exploitation of Public-Facing Application (GeoServer CVE-2024-36401; Zimbra CVE-2025-66376); Valid Accounts via VPN auth bypass (Check Point, PAN‑OS).
Persistence/Privilege: Webshells on IIS/SharePoint; creation of Zimbra app passwords; rogue OAuth app-only access via Microsoft Graph (Project CAV3RN).
Discovery/Lateral: Living-off-the-land (BITS, certutil, PowerShell), router SNMP/OID abuse, credential harvesting from email/AD, VPN session hijack.
Command & Control: Residential/SOHO proxying; Outlook calendar dead drops; SSH tunnels; DNS AAAA data channels.
Impact (ICS): PLC program download/online edits; VNC abuse of HMIs causing setpoint changes/loss of view; MMS/104 parser crashes (DoS).

outlook72h: Expect continued mass scanning and opportunistic exploitation of remote access gateways (Check Point, PAN‑OS) and collaboration stacks (SharePoint, Zimbra). Prioritize patching and log review on internet-exposed assets. OT library advisories (libIEC61850/lib60870) may prompt targeted testing; isolate and monitor MMS/104 services for malformed traffic and crashes. Increased hacktivist probing of exposed VNC/remote services on HMIs likely around weekends/holidays; validate no HMIs are publicly reachable. Proxies/botnets (residential/SOHO) continue to mask actor origins; tune geo/ASN anomaly detections for admin authentications.
